title: lint(dashboard-filter-binding-unknown): its explanation says a dateRange binding on a dashboard with no dateRange is always reported, but a globalFilters entry named dateRange is a declared filter there
body:
domain:spec#2 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmSduNGC2SZXszyrNut

Filing gate: ① a should-fix named by the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review of PR #29370 (#29213), record 6578522383, kept out of that PR to hold it to its claimed surface. ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets it.

## What the text says

`packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`, rule `dashboard-filter-binding-unknown` (≈L407–409 on `main`): "A `dateRange` key on a dashboard that declares no `dateRange` is reported the same way: there is no date range for it to bind."

## Why it may be wrong

The same explanation's first paragraph says the names a widget may bind are each `globalFilters` entry under its `name` (its `field` when unnamed) and the reserved `dateRange` when the dashboard declares `dateRange`. PR #29370 keeps a `globalFilters` entry keyed `dateRange` ACCEPTED on a dashboard that declares no `dateRange` (the seat's answer to that PR's open question, Q1 = A: it is a working filter there). On such a dashboard a widget's `filterBindings.dateRange` names a declared filter, so "is reported the same way" reads false, or the rule reports a valid binding. Not measured: which of the two it is.

## Wanted

Measure `dashboard-filter-binding-unknown` on a dashboard with no `dateRange`, a `globalFilters` entry named `dateRange`, and a widget binding `dateRange`. If the rule accepts it, correct the sentence (prose only). If it reports it, that is a false positive on a valid board: fix the rule to read the declared name set, with a test.

Reader who acts: the `packages/lint` owner (`domain:spec` by the anchoring rule).

Dedupe: searched `dashboard-filter-binding-unknown dateRange`, `filterBindings dateRange globalFilters`: only #29213 / PR #29370 and #29023. **New.**
